title: There is no library/ folder, so no written requirements or architecture notes exist for agents to follow.
evidence:
$ ls library
ls: library: No such file or directory
why_it_matters: Without written requirements, every agent session re-guesses how the app is meant to work, which is how features drift.
remediation: Run get-started-stinger in init mode to scaffold library/, then add one knowledge doc for the auth flow in apps/web.
verified_by: Listed the repository root and searched for any docs/ or library/ folder.

title: No AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md tells coding agents the project's rules.
evidence:
$ ls AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md .cursor/rules
ls: AGENTS.md: No such file or directory
why_it_matters: Agents will not know to run the tests or to keep server code out of client components.
remediation: Add AGENTS.md at the repo root with the test command (pnpm test), the lint command, and the rule that apps/web/app/**/actions.ts must call requireUser().

title: CI runs lint but never runs the test suite.
evidence:
- run: pnpm lint
      # - run: pnpm test   (commented out)
why_it_matters: Broken behavior can merge to main because nothing checks it before merge.
remediation: Uncomment the pnpm test step in .github/workflows/ci.yml line 30 and make it a required status check on main.
verified_by: Read the workflow file end to end.

title: No CODEOWNERS file, so nobody is asked to review changes to payment code.
evidence:
$ ls .github/CODEOWNERS
ls: .github/CODEOWNERS: No such file or directory
why_it_matters: Changes to billing can merge with only the author's review.
remediation: Add .github/CODEOWNERS with apps/api/billing/ owned by the billing lead.
verified_by: Searched the three paths GitHub reads CODEOWNERS from.

title: Next.js 15.5.2 and Node 22 are current supported releases.
why_it_matters: No action needed; recorded so later dimensions know the versions.
